concepts.def: (a+b)ⁿ = Σ C(n,r) a^(n-r) b^r for non-negative integer n.
C(n,r) = n!/[r!(n-r)!] counts ways to choose r from n.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between an arithmetic and a geometric sequence?
options: Arithmetic sequences only use whole numbers and geometric sequences use decimals.
Arithmetic has a constant difference between terms; geometric has a constant ratio.
x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.
Arithmetic sequences involve only addition and geometric sequences only multiplication, so 1, 2, 4 is arithmetic.
Eventually a term will be so small it equals 0.
It reaches 0 at the millionth term.
Arithmetic sequences only use whole numbers and geometric sequences use decimals.
No — it approaches 0 as the limit but no term is ever exactly 0.

mcqs.q: What is the value of x^0 (for x not equal to zero)?
options: x^0 equals 0 because raising something to the zero gives nothing.
1 — any non-zero number to the power of zero equals 1.
x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.
Arithmetic sequences only use whole numbers and geometric sequences use decimals.
